text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division this weekend. All games kick off at 1330 GMT on Saturday.

Hamburg's caretaker coach Rolf Schehr faces a daunting first game in charge against reigning champions returning to form just in time for next week's European Cup final. Seven players absent for Hamburg through injury or suspension.

Bochum slipped up badly in their quest for a UEFA Cup place last week, their 6-2 defeat by Moenchengladbach allowing rivals 1860 Munich to move to within a point. They should be favourites for maximum points in this match, however, against a team depleted by injury and already relegated.

Duisburg coach Friedhelm Funkel is expected to stick to the side which beat Stuttgart last week, even though striker Markus Marin has recovered from a back injury. Moenchengladbach also expected to stick to last week's winning line-up.

Libero Lothar Matthaeus doubtful for Bayern because of a muscle strain while Thomas Strunz is definitely out with a back injury. Stuttgart welcome back Andreas Buck and Marco Haber. Fans in the Olympic Stadium could be treated to a goal festival -- this match has ended 5-3 twice in the past five years.

Promoted Bielefeld have secured top-flight survival while Rostock still have mathematical chance of going down. Hansa may be unsettled by rumours swirling around coach Frank Pagelsdorf who has been linked with moves to several clubs.

Meaningless match more likely to be remembered for its party atmosphere than anything taking place on the pitch. Schalke have secured European soccer for next season thanks to Wednesday's UEFA Cup triumph while Freiburg are already relegated.

Crunch game for two UEFA Cup candidates. Thomas Haessler may return after long injury layoff for Karlsruhe, who can also welcome back Thorsten Fink and Dirk Schuster from suspension. Munich still without injured top scorer Bernhard Winkler.
Duesseldorf must win to have any chance of staying in the Bundesliga but prospects look bleak as Bremen have won their last three home games.

Lerkusen face local rivals Cologne deprived of Danish midfielder Jan Heintze because of injury. His countryman Hendrik Andersen is doubtful for Cologne with a swollen ankle. Leverkusen beat Cologne 4-2 in the first half of the season. Anything less than a repeat performance could hand the title to Bayern.
